htmlTitle: How many square metres can you afford? — housing affordability in Europe and the United States
metaDescription: Type your net income and see how many square metres you could buy or rent in 8,489 European municipalities and 3,043 US counties: 22 million European listings from the ESPON HOUSE4ALL dataset behind the 2026 TU Wien study, and 3.6 million American sales from Redfin, with HUD incomes and rents.
ogDescription: Your income, 11,532 places in Europe and the United States: how many square metres a third of it buys or rents, built from open data and honest about what does not compare.
imageAlt: Two maps side by side, Europe by municipality and the United States by county, dotted in five shades from light to dark, dark where a third of the average income buys the least space
title: How many square metres can you afford?
ldDescription: An interactive calculator and map of housing affordability in square metres: net income in, affordable square metres out, for 8,489 municipalities and 1,251 NUTS 3 regions in 31 European countries (ESPON HOUSE4ALL, the dataset behind Sielker and Banabak 2026, Journal of Maps) and for 3,043 counties in the United States (Redfin sales, HUD income and rent, Freddie Mac rates).
ldDatasetName: Housing affordability by European municipality and US county, 2024–2026
ldDatasetDescription: Per-municipality (LAU) sale price and rent per square metre, mean equivalised disposable income 2024, national mortgage rate and the square metres a third of the local mean income buys on a 30-year mortgage or rents, for 89,601 municipalities in 34 European countries, extracted from the public ESPON HOUSE4ALL feature service (TU Wien, InAtlas, MCRIT) on 14 September 2026; and per-county median price per square metre from Redfin sales of June 2025 to May 2026, HUD FY2025 median family income, HUD FY2025 fair market rent by bedroom count and the Freddie Mac 30-year fixed rate, for 3,043 US counties.
